results.title: IT trends 2025: 12 must‑watch IT topics | Wavestone
results.content: As organizations accelerate digital initiatives to seize new growth opportunities, technology leaders face the dual challenge of driving innovation while managing risk. Embedding resilience at the core of a digital strategy enables organizations to quickly adapt to emerging risks, protect critical assets, and ensure operational continuity. Advanced technologies such as automated data masking, encryption, and AI-driven compliance monitoring are critical to meeting these requirements while maintaining customer trust and avoiding costly penalties. Organizations investing early in advanced in these technologies can gain a decisive edge, particularly in businesses where wireless, reliability and automation are keys for a competitive advantage. Organizations that invest now in quantum research, pilot projects, and ecosystem partnerships position themselves as leaders in industries where complex optimization problems or long-term data security are critical. By focusing on user-centric data models and creating economies based on digital assets, businesses are unlocking possibilities for new revenue streams and collaborative ecosystems.

results.content: AI can help “sift through those vast data sets to identify patterns, anomalies, and use that data for these risk assessments.” Revisit vendor contracts and consider building clauses for shared tariff responsibilities or performance-based cost adjustments (Anchin, 2025). ### IT is moving beyond project-based digital change to become an orchestrator of enterprise resilience, helping to embed risk management into every capability, from APIs and data platforms to AI agents and security controls. There will be temptation to push further into AI capabilities and pursue agentic automation of enterprise-risk-oriented tasks with automated policy enforcement. Cultivate a viewpoint of risk management as a competitive differentiator that helps your organization build trust, develop clear ethical AI alignment, and deliver on ESG considerations. At their core, agents will be limited in capability by underlying AI models and whether AI vendors can continue to make strides in improving intelligence or falter in making progress because of hindrances like power supply, access to GPUs, or a lack of new training data.

results.title: [PDF] Software Modernization Implementation Plan, FY25-26 - DoD CIO
results.content: The FY23-24 Software Modernization Implementation Plan focused on collective actions that enabled the DoD to modernize the infrastructure, platforms, processes, workforce skills, and DoD culture for delivering secure software to the warfighter. Software is a critical element of systems in the Department of Defense (DoD) and the ability to deliver software at the speed of relevance requires continued software modernization by executing the tasks identified in this FY25-26 implementation plan. The implementation plan aligns with DoD’s Fulcrum which is the Department’s IT Advancement Strategy to optimize the use of innovative products, improve IT user experiences, and enhance operational effectiveness by identifying tasks that focus on modernizing weapons systems and legacy business systems, and improving financial operations with cloud and software factories. In FY23-24, DoD developed cATO evaluation criteria and implementation guidance to strengthen security, improve risk management, and accelerate cybersecurity approvals; continued to mature and increase adoption of the Software Acquisition Pathway; and introduced eight new software engineering work roles to the DoD Cyber Workforce Framework.
